service.description: Open a merge request of a source branch into a target branch (the default branch when empty), as the current user, who may push to the repository. A draft is not merged until it is marked ready. Its number is the repository's next from 1; its head, merge base and mergeability are read now. Only one open request per source and target. Webhooks get a merge_request event (opened).

A merge request for its viewers: its fields, the repository's default merge method, its reviewers (with their names, whether their approval is of the current head, and whether it counts: only approvals of users who may push count, get#MergeRequestApprovals), the head's checks, the target's branch rules and what keeps it from merging now (missing), and what the current user may do.

parameter.name: missingList
parameter.description: Why it cannot merge now; empty when it can

service.description: Change an open or draft merge request: the title, description, target branch, draft (a draft marked ready opens), merge method and whether the source branch goes after the merge. By its author or a user with update. A new target is checked for mergeability again.
Who reviews a merge request: replace them with userIdList, or add and remove some. A reviewer kept keeps their review; one added is requested. Not the author. By its author or a user with update.

A review of a merge request at its current head by the current user, who may view the repository: approve, request changes or comment, with a summary. Only a user who may push (update on the repository) approves; a viewer comments or requests changes. The author does not approve their own. A reviewer not requested becomes one. Webhooks get a merge_request event (reviewed).
Close a merge request without merging it. By its author or a user with update.
Open a closed merge request again, when its source branch is still there and the repository is not archived; its mergeability is checked again. By its author or a user with update.

Merge an open merge request by its method (the one given, else its own, else the repository's default) once the target's branch rules are met: the approvals required (of the current head when the rule dismisses stale ones; only those of users who may push count), the required checks successful on the head, a method they allow. Needs update on the repository; refused on a conflict. The request becomes merged with the target's new head; its source branch is deleted when asked (kept, with a message, when its branch rules refuse). Webhooks get a merge_request event (merged).

parameter.name: message
parameter.description: Of the merge commit or squash

service.description: For a viewer of the repository, the approvals of a merge request that count toward the target's branch rules: approved (of the current head when the rules dismiss stale approvals) by a user who may push to the repository now, decided as that user. merge#MergeRequest counts the same way.

Merge requests of the repositories the current user may view, last updated first, paged: by repository, status, author, reviewer, the ones waiting for a user's review, target branch and text in the title. Each with its repository, branches, author and reviewers' names, mergeability and the head's combined check state.

parameter.name: waitingForUserId
parameter.description: Requested reviews of this user not yet given, of open requests

service.description: What a merge request changes, for review: the commits and each file's diff, as get#GitCompare gives them (the moqui-diff html and hunks of numbered lines), from its target to its source while it is open, and from its recorded merge base to its recorded head once merged or closed. For its viewers.

Read a merge request's source head, merge base and mergeability again (a trial merge into its target); merged when the target already holds the head. For refresh#MergeRequests and the services that change a request's branches.

The framework's ref-update gitECA rule (Git.gitecas.xml): a branch moved. Each open merge request whose source it is takes the new head (its approvals set back to requested when the target's branch rules dismiss stale ones; webhooks get a merge_request event, synchronize), and each whose source or target it is is checked for mergeability again, and is merged when the target holds its head. One that fails is logged and the others are still refreshed.
A merge_request event of a merge request (opened, updated, ready, reviewed, synchronize, closed, reopened, merged) to the repository's webhooks. A failure is logged; the change it reports stands.
